etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin ex (“to delete, to cross out”) and tenuatus, past participle of tenuare (“to make thin”) + Middle English -ing. By surface analysis, ex- +‎ tenuate +‎ -ing.
senses: present participle and gerund of extenuate
That attenuates or lessens the seriousness of something, e.g. by providing a mitigating excuse for it.
